svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "Sound waves (vibrations of air molecules) are collected by the pinna and funnelled down the ear canal."], [2.5, "The sound waves make the eardrum vibrate at the same frequency as the sound."], [4.5, "The eardrum passes the vibrations to the ossicles: malleus, then incus, then stapes. Acting as levers, they amplify the vibrations."], [7, "The stapes pushes the oval window in and out, making pressure waves in the fluid inside the cochlea; the round window bulges out to let the fluid move."], [10, "The pressure waves move the hairs of sensory hair cells in the cochlea. The hair cells send nerve impulses along the auditory nerve to the brain, which interprets them as sound."]]
svg.title: The human ear in section
svg.desc: Section through the right ear seen from the front: pinna, ear canal, eardrum, middle ear with malleus, incus and stapes, oval and round windows, Eustachian tube, and the inner ear with semicircular canals, vestibule, cochlea and auditory nerve, inside the temporal bone.
svg.text: Section through the right ear, seen from the front (outside of the head on the left). Not to scale: the middle and inner ear are enlarged.

g.data-info: The middle and inner ear lie protected inside this bone.
Flap of skin and cartilage that collects sound waves and funnels them into the ear canal.
Tube that carries sound waves to the eardrum. Its hairs and wax trap dust and microorganisms.
Air-filled cavity in the skull bone containing the three ossicles.
Connects the middle ear to the throat; opening it (yawning, swallowing) equalises the air pressure on both sides of the eardrum.
Thin, tight membrane that vibrates when sound waves hit it, at the same frequency as the sound.
First ossicle; attached to the eardrum, so it vibrates with it.
Middle ossicle; passes vibrations from the malleus to the stapes.
Smallest bone in the body. Its footplate fits in the oval window. The three ossicles act as levers that amplify the vibrations.
The vestibulocochlear nerve: carries impulses from the cochlea (and the balance organs) to the brain, where they are interpreted as sound.
Three fluid-filled canals at right angles to each other; they detect movements of the head and help with balance, not hearing.
Fluid-filled chamber linking the semicircular canals and the cochlea; detects the position of the head.
Membrane between the middle ear and the inner ear. The stapes pushes it in and out, making pressure waves in the fluid of the cochlea.
Membrane below the oval window that bulges out as the oval window is pushed in, so the cochlear fluid can move.
Coiled, fluid-filled tube lined with sensory hair cells. Pressure waves in the fluid move the hairs, and the hair cells send impulses: different parts respond to different pitches.

g.text: 1 The pinna funnels sound waves into the ear canal
3 The ossicles vibrate and amplify the vibrations
4 The stapes makes pressure waves in the cochlear fluid
5 Hair cells send impulses along the auditory nerve
